title: Ibuprofen — general information
content: Ibuprofen is an over-the-counter nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory (NSAID) used for general pain, inflammation, and fever. It's available as tablets, capsules, and liquid gels. For dosing or interaction questions, a pharmacist consultation is required.

title: Acetaminophen — general information
content: Acetaminophen is an over-the-counter pain reliever and fever reducer, available as tablets, caplets, and liquid. It works differently from NSAIDs like ibuprofen. Dosing questions should go to a pharmacist.

title: Aspirin — general information
content: Aspirin is an over-the-counter NSAID used for pain, fever, and, under a doctor's guidance, heart-health purposes. It's sold in regular and low-dose tablet forms. A pharmacist can advise on which form applies to you.

title: Antihistamine (loratadine) — general information
content: Loratadine is a non-drowsy, over-the-counter antihistamine used for seasonal allergy symptoms such as sneezing and itchy eyes. It's available in tablet and liquid form.

title: Cough syrup — general information
content: Over-the-counter cough syrups come in suppressant and expectorant formulas for dry versus productive coughs. A pharmacist can help identify which type fits your symptoms.

title: Antacid — general information
content: Antacids are over-the-counter products used for occasional heartburn and indigestion, available as chewable tablets or liquid. They work by neutralizing stomach acid.

title: Vitamin D — general information
content: Vitamin D supplements are available over the counter in various strengths and support bone and immune health. A pharmacist can help you understand the strength options available.

title: Multivitamin — general information
content: Multivitamins are over-the-counter daily supplements combining multiple vitamins and minerals, available in adult, prenatal, and children's formulas.

title: Hydrocortisone cream — general information
content: Hydrocortisone cream is an over-the-counter topical product used for minor skin irritation, itching, and rashes. It's applied directly to the affected area.

title: Saline nasal spray — general information
content: Saline nasal spray is an over-the-counter, medication-free option for nasal congestion and dryness, safe for regular use including in children.

title: Electrolyte solution — general information
content: Electrolyte solutions and powders are over-the-counter products used to help replace fluids and minerals, commonly used during illness or after exercise.

title: Melatonin — general information
content: Melatonin is an over-the-counter sleep-support supplement available in various strengths and forms, including tablets and gummies.

title: Probiotic — general information
content: Probiotic supplements contain live cultures marketed to support digestive health, available in capsule, chewable, and powder forms.

title: Sunscreen — general information
content: Sunscreen products are available over the counter in a range of SPF levels and formats, including lotion, spray, and stick.

title: Hand sanitizer — general information
content: Hand sanitizer is an over-the-counter product for reducing germs on hands when soap and water aren't available, typically alcohol-based.

title: Bandages and first aid — general information
content: We carry a range of adhesive bandages, gauze, and first aid supplies for minor cuts and scrapes, available in the first aid aisle or online.

title: Blood pressure monitor — general information
content: Home blood pressure monitors are available as arm-cuff or wrist-cuff devices. Staff can help you choose a model, but readings should be reviewed with your doctor.

title: Thermometer — general information
content: We carry digital, forehead, and ear thermometers for home use, suitable for both adults and children.

title: Glucose test strips — general information
content: Glucose test strips are available for common home glucose meter brands. A pharmacist can help confirm compatibility with your specific meter.

title: Over-the-counter pain relief — general overview
content: Over-the-counter pain relief options include NSAIDs like ibuprofen and aspirin, and non-NSAID options like acetaminophen. Which one is appropriate depends on individual health factors — a pharmacist consultation is recommended for that decision.

title: Over-the-counter versus prescription medication
content: Over-the-counter medications can be purchased without a doctor's prescription, while prescription medications require a valid prescription from a licensed provider and are dispensed by our pharmacy team.

title: Generic versus brand-name medication
content: Generic medications contain the same active ingredient, strength, and dosage form as their brand-name equivalents and are typically lower cost. Availability can be confirmed with the pharmacy team.
